πρό-κλησις , εως, Ion.
ιος, ἡ,
A.calling forth, challenge,
“μουνομαχίη ἐκ προκλήσιος”
Hdt. 5.1
, cf. 9.75 ; “π. ἔφυγε”
Plu. Marc. 2
.
2. sounding of the advance,
Opp.
“ἀνάκλησις, προκλήσεις σάλπιγγος”
J. BJ 2.20.7
.
II. invitation, offer, proposal,
“τὴν π. ἡμῶν οὐκ ἐδέχεσθε”
Th. 3.64
, cf. Arist. Pol. 1292a29 , etc.; “π. ποιησάμενοι”
D.H. 7.39
; “προτιθέναι”
App. BC 1.4
.
III. as law-term, formal challenge or wager, offered by either party to his opponent, for the purpose of bringing disputed points to issue, such as a challenge to the opponent to let his slaves be tortured to give evidence against him, or an offer of one's own slaves to be tortured, Lys. 4.15 , D. 37.40 ; challenge or offer to take an oath with respect to the matter at issue, Arist. Rh. 1377a20 ; π. προκαλεῖσθαι to make such a challenge,
D. 59.124 : c. dupl. acc., “προκαλοῦνται πρόκλησιν ἡμᾶς ὡς οὐ δεξομένους”
Id. 37.12
; “οὐ δέξεσθαι τὴν π.”
Id. 40.10
; φεύγειν to decline it,
Antipho 6.27 ; μαρτυρεῖν to appeal to it,
D. 45.15 .
IV. titillation, stimulation,
Aret. CA 1.2 , al.
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
